name: Hayabusa2
first: Second asteroid sample return (Ryugu, 2020); first artificial impact crater on an asteroid; first subsurface asteroid material returned to Earth
description: JAXA's follow-on to the original Hayabusa. Launched 2014-12-03, Hayabusa2 reached carbonaceous near-Earth asteroid (162173) Ryugu on 2018-06-27 after a 3.5-year low-thrust ion cruise + Earth gravity assist. Surface operations 2018–2019: two touchdown-and-go sample collections bracketing a Small Carry-on Impactor experiment (2019-04-05) that excavated a 14 m crater for the second sample. Three MINERVA-II rovers returned the first surface images from an asteroid; the DLR/CNES MASCOT lander operated for 17 hours. Sample return capsule reentry over Woomera on 2020-12-05 delivered 5.4 g of pristine Ryugu material — the first asteroid sample with subsurface stratigraphy. Extended mission: flyby of (98943) 2001 CC21 in 2026-07; rendezvous with fast-rotating (1998 KY26) targeted for 2031-07.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: H-IIA 202 from Tanegashima begins the 3.5-year cruise to asteroid Ryugu.

events.label: EARTH FLYBY
events.note: Earth gravity assist phases the rendezvous orbit.

events.label: RYUGU ARRIVAL
events.note: Hover at 20 km — start of 1.5-year proximity operations including sample collection.

events.label: EARTH RETURN
events.note: Sample capsule lands in Woomera, Australia with 5.4 g of Ryugu material.

events.label: 1998 KY26 RENDEZVOUS
events.note: Planned rendezvous with fast-rotating asteroid (1998 KY26).
